correctness.rationale: A generic one-parameter subtorus of the row-column scaling torus has pairwise distinct coordinate weights, so the projective fixed locus consists exactly of the mn coordinate matrices. All have rank one, hence every nontrivial determinantal rank locus has the same fixed locus and therefore Euler characteristic mn. For the maximal-minor locus, Thom--Porteous applied to O(-1)^m -> O^n gives class c_{n-m+1}(O^n-O(-1)^m), whose coefficient is binomial(n,m-1). The exact ratio R(m,n+1)/R(m,n)=n/(n-m+2) proves strict monotonicity for m>=3, and the displayed base values exhaust every comparison case. The bundled checker replays the general determinantal product, specialization, ratios, and fixed-point count over a broad finite range.

value.rationale: Generic determinantal varieties are basic singular models in projective algebraic geometry. The rank-independent Euler value mn gives a uniform topological baseline across the entire rank tower, while maximal-minor projective degree grows with aspect ratio. The theorem pinpoints exactly where enumerative complexity falls below, equals, or exceeds this fixed topological complexity, with only two nontrivial equality formats. The result is an all-parameter structural classification rather than a finite table.
